#1658. Gila explains how he went from ‘rock bottom’ at Lazio to joining Milan: “More kindness”

Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.

Gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services. In his first season, however, he only got 765 minutes on the pitch and didn’t play a single game in the second half of the campaign.

The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time. The growth only continued from there, resulting in Milan paying good money for him in the summer.

In his long interview with AC Milan for the interview series The Chamber, Gila discussed his initial struggles in Italy, hitting ‘rock bottom’ in his first season with Lazio. A psychologist and a changed mindset helped him get through it all.

When you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

“In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

“That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

“So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

“Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”

#1657. Spain 2-3 England: Thomas Tuchel’s side set new all-time winning record after “complete performance” in Nations League

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 12:57, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 13:21

England have set a new all-time winning record after beating world champions Spain 3-2 in their final UEFA Nations League group fixture on Sunday.

The Three Lions knew that they had to beat the 2026 World Cup winners at Estadio Metropolitano on Madrid if they were to finish top of League A Group 3 on goal difference.

Thomas Tuchel’s side entered the half-time interval in front courtesy of a converted penalty from 2026 Ballon d’Or winner and England’s top goalscorer Harry Kane, who has set yet another scoring record.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased England’s lead with two goals in the space of just four minutes, putting the visitors firmly in control.

However, Elliot Anderson was sent off just six minutes after England’s third goal for a last-man pull-back on Lamine Yamal inside the penalty area, with Mikel Oyarzabal netting the resulting spot kick.

The momentum then shifted into Spain’s favour and substitute Nico Williams gave the hosts hope of a late comeback with a 75th-minute strike, but the Three Lions admirably dug deep to hold on for a crucial victory.

Victory for England means they have now won 10 consecutive away matches across all competitions for the first time in their history.

Success has also confirmed that England finish top of League A Group 3, progressing to the Nations League quarter-finals where they will face one of the runners-up in League A, with a guaranteed second leg at home.

Furthermore, England’s memorable night in Madrid saw them end Spain’s world-record 43-game unbeaten run spanning across almost three years.

After the match, Tuchel acknowledged that his team’s performance against La Roja was their best since he became England head coach in January 2025.

“Yes,” he told reporters. “Given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. That was a very complete performance and the best I’ve had so far.

“What a performance we put out there to be deservedly 3-0 up after 60 to 65 minutes. Of course the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and characteristic of the game. Thirty minutes [of defending] against Spain in Spain feels like three hours!

“This was, of course, a statement victory and the statement and significance of it was that it was deserved.

“The result followed the performance. It was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness and it was on the highest level football-wise, on all aspects of the game.

“We did everything that needs to be done together – the deep buildup, the high press and attacking defensive phases.

England’s next match will be the first leg of their Nations League quarter-final tie, scheduled between March 25 and March 27 next year.

The Three Lions will discover their opponent when the draw is made on Friday at 11am UK time.

England cannot be drawn against Spain again, but they could face Group A1 runners-up Belgium, or one of three teams from Group A2 (Netherlands, Greece or Germany) or Group A4 (Portugal, Denmark or Norway).

The official quarter-final lineup will be confirmed after the final round of fixtures on Tuesday.

#1656. Spain 2-3 England: Harry Kane equals 78-year Tom Finney scoring record in Nations League win

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 13:20

England captain Harry Kane has etched his name into the record books once again after scoring in Sunday’s 3-2 triumph over Spain in the UEFA Nations League.

The 2026 Ballon d’Or winner made his 127th international appearance at Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, just three days after surpassing Peter Shilton as England’s most-capped player against Croatia.

On the stroke of half time, Kane fired England into a deserved half-time lead with a converted penalty after being felled by Spain defender Pau Cubarsi.

In doing so, England’s No.9 has now equalled an impressive scoring feat which had been unmatched since 1948.

Indeed, Kane has scored in each of his last seven international away matches dating back to June 2025, becoming the first Three Lions player to achieve this feat since legend Tom Finney between September 1946 and May 1948.

This record excludes neutral venues and therefore does not include the goals Kane scored at the 2026 World Cup where England finished third.

Kane’s away scoring streak began with goals in four successive World Cup qualifiers against Andorra, Serbia, Latvia and Albania, helping the Three Lions complete their qualification campaign with a perfect record.

The Bayern Munich striker has since netted in all three of his away matches with England in the Nations League against Czech Republic, Croatia and now Spain.

Kane has scored a total of 10 goals across those seven away games, while he has also extended his all-time scoring record with England to 93.

The last time Kane failed to make the net ripple for England at a non-neutral away venue came against Greece in November 2024 (3-0 Nations League win).

Kane will endeavour to surpass Finney outright and extend his scoring run on the road to eight games when England enter the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027.

Reacting to England’s memorable win in Madrid, Kane told reporters: “I think that’s as big as it gets outside of a major tournament, for sure.

“We spoke before the Nations League campaign that we want to use these games to really improve, really stamp our identity on how we want to move going forward.

“No better game than Spain away after they’re unbeaten in 40-odd games to show that, and what a performance. Up until the red card it was dominant, clinical, high intensity and they couldn’t live with it.

“It was a shame [Elliot Anderson’s] red card happened because I think [the scoreline] could have been more and that’s been our mindset. That it doesn’t matter what the scoreline is – we go and we go and we go. You saw that out there tonight.

“In the end, we had to find a different way to win with the red card, obviously, and it was similar to a Mexico feeling where we’re digging deep.

“But when you can do both sides of the game like that it means you’re a very good team, so credit to everyone involved. It’s been a great campaign so far and we can end the year with our heads held high.”

Kane has scored in all six of England’s Nations League matches in the 2026-27 campaign, netting a competition-high eight goals in total to put him firmly in the frame to win the Golden Boot.

The 47-capped Morocco international can play on either wing but is primarily used as an attacking midfielder, and has become a key part of Stuttgart's attacking unit.

The 22-year-old has had a fairly slow start to this campaign, scoring twice in 15 appearances, 10 of which were starts.

El Khannouss' talent is clear to see though, and the dynamic attacker produced 16 goals and assists for Stuttgart last season, also providing two assists for Leicester before his move.

The Moroccan was heavily linked with a switch to Brighton in the summer, but the deal ultimately fell through, and now several Premier League clubs are interested.

That's according to Ekrem Konur, who has revealed Liverpool alongside Leeds and Newcastle are chasing a deal for El Khannouss, with Galatasaray also closely monitoring the situation.

Liverpool are currently well-stocked for wide options but lack a true alternative to Florian Wirtz in the number 10 role, a gap that El Khannouss could easily fill for the Reds.

Konur doesn't reveal a potential fee, but with interest so high a bidding war could ensue, driving the 22-year-old's price higher.

Khannouss would be a sensible addition for the Reds and is definitely a player to keep an eye on heading into the winter window.

#1654. 'It's a LIE': Bullish Morgan Rogers hits back at claims Cole Palmer isn't committed to England as Three Lions star appears to suggest Thomas Tuchel is 'wrong' for questioning Chelsea team-mate

Published: 18:35 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 12 November 2026

Morgan Rogers has rubbished questions around team-mate and friend Cole Palmer's commitment to England after the Chelsea star was left out of the latest squad.

After missing out on selection for the World Cup, Palmer was called up to the group for the first international break of the season as he continued to monitor his fitness, but dropped out of the squad.

It meant he was again ignored when it came to selection for this fortnight's Nations League games against Croatia and Spain, with manager Thomas Tuchel saying Palmer 'misses too many opportunities to impress' him.

The events have led to criticism of Palmer, who scored for England in the final of Euro 2024, but Rogers has moved to defend his friend.

'It's a lie,' Rogers, who was speaking after starting and scoring for England in their 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday, said on BBC 5 Live. 'He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

'We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he's been managing them injuries ever since. He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100 per cent himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. Of course he does, who wouldn't?

Morgan Rogers (right) has rubbished questions around Cole Palmer's (left) commitment to the England team

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel (right) said Palmer 'misses too many opportunities to impress' him

'But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 to 15 years, (so) he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.

'It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it. But it's something he has to deal with but I can assure you he wants to be here and he wants to play for his country.'

Tuchel has accepted that Palmer is 'no exception' to being 'desperate' to wanting to play for England.

But the German claimed he has largely opted to stick with much of the group he ran with in the last international break, despite calling up Jobe Bellingham, James Hill, and Josh King – who plays in Palmer's position – for the first time.

'It's not personal,' the Three Lions boss said on the 24-year-old's omission. 'And of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country, but the competition is on and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.'

Rogers, though, is desperate to see Palmer back in an England shirt.

'What a player he is,' he added. 'What a person he is and it's someone you want to see in an England shirt.

'He's got so much quality, so much ability. We all know what we can do, what he's done, so of course we want to see him in an England shirt and hopefully sooner rather than later.'

#1653. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#1652. CorSport: RedBird could consider stock market listing of Milan’s new holding company

AC Milan’s new holding company, Milan Sports & Entertainment, could be publicly listed within five years according to a report.

Yesterday, RedBird announced the creation of a new holding company for the AC Milan project, named Milan Sports & Entertainment (MSE). The main goal is to have everything under one roof, from the football team to the new stadium and the NBA Europe project.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Cardinale himself said, there will be several new revenue streams that ultimately will benefit the football club, making it possible to invest more money in players and additional infrastructure. In short, it’s a big project and it could get even bigger.

According to Corriere dello Sport this morning, as cited by MilanNews, the launch of MSE proves that RedBird and Cardinale have a long-term plan for the club. A listing on the stock market cannot be ruled out within the next five years either, opening the company up to further investment.

Only two football clubs in Italy are publicly traded, namely Juventus and Lazio, meaning fans can effectively become shareholders. However, it should be noted that these shares rarely come with any real power, used more as a way of raising funds than anything else.

Outside of Italy, clubs like Borussia Dortmund and Manchester United are also publicly listed, so it’s not like Milan would be moving into uncharted territory.

#1651. Tottenham transfer news: Spurs ‘won’t panic buy’ in January as new striker pursuit is explained

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 13:41

Tottenham Hotspur are expected to accelerate their pursuit of a new striker during the January transfer window, according to a report.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side have struggled to convert chances so far this season, with only Sunderland (eight) and Nottingham Forest (nine) netting fewer goals than Spurs (10) in the Premier League after 10 games.

Spurs were unable to make the net ripple when they lost 1-0 at Leeds United before the international break, a result that ended a positive three-match winning run.

Dominic Solanke and summer signing Omar Marmoush have alternated leading the line under De Zerbi, but the pair have scored just three goals between them this season.

In fact, no Spurs player has scored more than two goals this term, with Solanke one of four men along with Conor Gallagher, Jan Paul van Hecke and Ben Davies who has netted multiple goals.

Spurs’ struggles in front of goal come at a time when Richarlison – the club’s top scorer with 11 PL goals last season – has been exiled from the senior squad after requesting to leave in the summer.

TEAMtalk reports that Bournemouth star Eli Junior Kroupi is a player ‘loved’ by De Zerbi, but his valuation between £80m and £100m could prove to be a major stumbling block for a club who spent in excess of £300m in the summer.

Spurs have since been on the lookout for alternative centre-forward options ahead of the New Year, with Freiburg frontman Igor Matanovic viewed as a possible target.

The 6ft 4in Croatia international has been in prolific form so far this season, scoring eight goals in 16 games across all competitions.

Journalist Ben Jacobs has revealed that Matanovic is indeed "one name" on Tottenham’s radar, but it remains to be seen whether they will push for the 23-year-old in January or wait until next summer.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, Jacobs said: “I think they could go for one [a striker] in January if the right target presents itself.

“It’s a shame how the Richarlison situation has panned out. Igor Matanovic is one name, as I exclusively revealed, that Tottenham like. They may look for something a little bit more short-term, like a loan. The same for Manchester United.

“If they can’t find the right target, or maybe someone with a bit more experience within the Premier League, then they can reassess in the summer.

“What they won’t want to do is necessarily go all in and panic buy in January for someone on a long-term contract, instead of just biding their time and waiting it out.”

Spurs could face competition from Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United for Matanovic, who is believed to be valued in the region of £50m.

Freiburg are in no rush to part ways with Matanovic, who remains a key player and is under contract at the Bundesliga club until 2029.

Re-signing striker Will Lankshear from Middlesbrough has also been mooted for Spurs, but the Championship club have allegedly slapped a £70m price tag on the 21-year-old, just months after signing him in the summer for a deal worth up to £20m.

#1649. Liverpool have two confirmed deals in place, must complete both - opinion

Liverpool have two deals in place already. We believe both should be completed ASAP.

Liverpool must sort their defensive situation out as it's one that risks getting massively out of hand. And that'll take some work.

As things stand, there are only two centre-backs in the first-team squad who are contracted to the club beyond this season. One is Jeremy Jacquet and the other Giovanni Leoni.

Only one of those has actually finished 90 minutes for Liverpool. It is, in other words, a less-than-ideal situation and one which will give Julian Ward and company a real headache.

Virgil van Dijk is out of contract, of course, as is Joe Gomez. Ronald Araujo's loan will end, too, and that trims the squad down dramatically. Fortunately, there's a relatively easy way to fix things as Liverpool do have two centre-backs deals lined up and agreed.

Liverpool's centre-back double-dealsAraujo, of course, may not leave. Liverpool have the option to sign the defender for €55m from Barcelona as long as he wants to commit to the Reds. Marca is among those claiming he wants to do just that, even if Liverpool need to wait until the end of the season to actually trigger the option. It appears, though, that the club are in favour of signing Araujo and that he will be a centre-back option beyond this season.

Araujo, of course, may not leave. Liverpool have the option to sign the defender for €55m from Barcelona as long as he wants to commit to the Reds.

Marca is among those claiming he wants to do just that, even if Liverpool need to wait until the end of the season to actually trigger the option. It appears, though, that the club are in favour of signing Araujo and that he will be a centre-back option beyond this season.

As long as nothing changes between now and then, anyway.

And he’s not the only one with a clause. Jarell Quansah left Liverpool in 2025 but the centre-back may be on his way back. There’s a buy clause in the deal with Bayer Leverkusen - one for 2026 and one for 2027 (Liverpool Echo).

Liverpool didn’t trigger the one in 2026, of course, but may well do so in 2027. That was always going to be the more likely of the two clauses, anyway, and the timing couldn’t be more ideal for a homegrown centre-back re-joining the club.

The Reds, then, are in a difficult situation but it’s one that they have created some room for manoeuvring in.

#1648. Chelsea news: Thomas Tuchel BlueCo sack reaction revealed by Jorginho

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 13:55

Jorginho has revealed that Chelsea's squad disagreed with BlueCo's decision to sack Thomas Tuchel in 2022.

Tuchel is currently receiving widespread plaudits after his England team ended Spain's 43-game undefeated streak on Sunday evening.

England stormed into a three-goal lead inside an hour, before an Elliot Anderson red card contributed to the Three Lions having to see out a nervy end to the contest in Madrid.

The result has helped Tuchel rebuild his reputation in big games, but the German will forever regarded as a Chelsea legend after the club's Champions League triumph in 2021.

However, 15 months on from that success in Porto, Tuchel was sacked by Chelsea's new owners BlueCo.

Speaking on the 'Obi One Podcast' hosted by former Blues midfielder John Obi Mikel, Jorginho acknowledged that he and his teammates were left stunned by the decision.

Asked to describe the reaction of Chelsea's first-team squad and himself, Jorginho replied: "What?".

"Like this. We were like 'we didn't expect it'. We were not having the best results at that moment, but us, it was not the moment.

At the start of the 2022-23 campaign, Chelsea collected 10 points from their opening six matches in the Premier League.

However, it was a 1-0 defeat away in Dinamo Zagreb that led to Tuchel being sacked by BlueCo on the following morning.

BlueCo had only just signed known Tuchel favourite Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang to become the club's new number nine.

Since that decision on September 7, 2022, it has since been suggested that BlueCo wanted to appoint their own head coach, the indication being that they did not want a manager chosen by predecessor Roman Abramovich to remain at the helm if they were not fully aligned in their relationship and club strategy.

#1647. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1646. Ronaldinho remembers ‘wonderful’ time at Milan and derby goal: “It was special”

Ronaldinho spoke about his time at AC Milan and the winner scored against Inter in the derby, seeing as he’s preparing for a professional comeback in another derby.

Ronaldinho is about to make a spectacular comeback at the age of 46, set to start for the Serie C side Ravenna against Forli tomorrow. Besides being an investor in the club, the main motivation for the comeback appears to be to score his 300th career goal (currently at 299).

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

When interviewed by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the journalist was keen to point out that Ronaldinho scored his first goal in Italy in a derby. More specifically for Milan against Inter, leading the Rossoneri to a 1-0 win in 2008.

You scored your first goal in Italy in the Milan derby…

“Oh, sure, that goal against Inter while wearing the AC Milan shirt. It was my first goal in Italy, it was special, and I’ll certainly never forget it, especially because every time I return to Italy I’m practically always reminded of it.

“My time with AC Milan was wonderful, for everyone, for the people who greeted me, the goals, the memories. Now I want to make the people of Ravenna happy for their passion.”

“So many, so many. The goals, the training sessions, Milanello, that goal in the derby, my teammates, the victories. AC Milan is always a wonderful memory, no matter how you look at it.”

#1645. Thomas Frank's Crystal Palace in-tray: Three big issues new Eagles boss must solve to avoid relegation

By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 15:28

Crystal Palace are closing in on the appointment of Thomas Frank as their new head coach, according to The Athletic, with the former Tottenham Hotspur and Brentford boss expected to replace Pierre Sage at Selhurst Park.

The 53-year-old faces an enormous challenge after Palace collected just seven points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, leaving them at the foot of the table. He has only a handful of days to work with his new squad before Saturday's trip to Coventry City, making an immediate improvement essential.

Frank has plenty of rebuilding to do after his difficult spell in north London, but his successful seven-year stint at Brentford offers encouragement.

Sports Mole looks at three priorities that should dominate his in-tray in the first few months.

Frank's most urgent task will be to address a defence that has conceded 24 goals in just ten Premier League matches, the worst record in the division. Palace have also shipped eight goals from set pieces, including four during their current run of four consecutive defeats.

It is a problem that predates Sage's arrival, having also troubled Oliver Glasner, but Frank has a reputation for organising competitive sides and could bring some much-needed structure. At Brentford, he alternated between a 3-5-2 and 4-3-3, with the former potentially straightforward to implement given Palace's familiarity with a back three.

However, the personnel available to him remain a concern. Palace did not adequately replace Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi, while summer arrivals Takehiro Tomiyasu, Axel Disasi and 18-year-old Honest Ahanor have not necessarily provided the defensive stability required.

Disasi is a particularly interesting case. The Chelsea loanee has an opportunity to establish himself as a key figure, but Frank must decide whether he is the right partner for the existing defensive options or whether further recruitment is required.

Frank's Brentford teams were also particularly dangerous from dead-ball situations, ranking among the Premier League's best for set-piece expected goals during his time there. Bringing that same attention to detail to both boxes could make an immediate difference.

Adam Wharton's decline in influence has been another major frustration for Palace. Only a few months ago, the midfielder was attracting reported interest from Chelsea, Manchester City and Liverpool, having established himself as one of the most exciting young English players in the Premier League.

Now, the noise surrounding his future has quietened considerably. Wharton missed out on England's 2026 World Cup squad and has struggled to reproduce the performances that previously made him so highly rated.

His average performance rating has dropped from fourth-best among Palace players in 2025-26 to seventh this season, with his contribution in possession and defensive work both coming under scrutiny.

Some of those difficulties appear connected to the unfamiliar responsibilities he has been given under Sage. Wharton has struggled to track runners and protect the space in front of the defence, and while not known for his attacking prowess, his influence in transition and in the final third has waned, registering fewer accurate long balls and key passes per 90 in the Premier League.

Frank must find a role that allows the 22-year-old to dictate games without leaving him exposed defensively. Restoring Wharton's confidence and getting him closer to his previous level would represent a significant boost, both for Palace's survival hopes and his longer-term development.

Palace's problems in front of goal are not quite as severe as their defensive shortcomings, but Frank will need to address the uncertainty surrounding his centre-forward options.

Jean-Philippe Mateta wanted to leave during the summer and is approaching the final months of his contract, while an injury has already disrupted his campaign. The Frenchman has yet to score in the Premier League this season and has accumulated more red cards than goals, leaving his future increasingly uncertain.

Jorgen Strand Larsen has also struggled to convince since arriving, managing just one goal in eight league appearances. His record of 19 goals in 79 top-flight outings hardly suggests he is ready to become a reliable long-term replacement for Mateta.

Frank may therefore need to look beyond Selhurst Park when the January window opens. A reunion with Richarlison, who looks to be available from ex-club Spurs, is one possibility worth considering, particularly given the Brazilian's previous experience under the Dane.

Palace spent heavily on 11 summer arrivals, so chairman Steve Parish may be reluctant to sanction another significant recruitment drive. Nevertheless, losing Mateta without securing a dependable replacement would leave Frank with a major problem.

With Palace already facing a fight to climb away from the bottom of the table, Frank cannot afford to wait until January to make improvements.

Defensive organisation, Wharton's revival and a reliable goalscorer represent three clear priorities if he is to turn a troubled season around.

#1643. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

#1642. Cesc Fabregas to Man United: 'Truth' revealed on potential move to Old Trafford for exciting young coach

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 15:36, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 15:38

Como head coach Cesc Fabregas was reportedly discussed by Manchester United chiefs as a potential replacement for Michael Carrick.

Fabregas is regarded as one of the brightest young coaches in world football, with the 39-year-old hugely impressive since taking charge of Como.

The former midfielder has won 46, drawn 26 and lost 26 of his 98 matches in charge of Como since being appointed permanent head coach in July 2024.

The Italian club's fourth-placed finish in the 2025-26 Serie A campaign saw them qualify for this season's Champions League, and they have impressed in the competition this term, including a standout 9-1 victory over Lille last time out.

Como are currently fourth in the Serie A table, only six points behind the leaders Lazio, and the team's style of football under Fabregas has been excelllent.

Man United lost 4-1 to Como in the Champions League earlier this season, and it appears only a matter of time before Fabregas makes the move to a major club.

According to The Athletic, Fabregas' name was mentioned when Man United had an executive committee meeting on November 5.

The report claims that Man United CEO Omar Berrada is a huge fan of Fabregas and had seemingly pushed the Spaniard's name into the conversation.

However, talk on Fabregas 'did not develop into anything further', according to the publication, with the club ultimately switching their attention to Mauricio Pochettino.

Fabregas has a contract with Como until the summer of 2028, and his future is certainly one to watch given how impressive his team have been.

Pochettino will officially become Man United's new head coach on November 18, once his commitments with USA have concluded.

The Argentine's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions will be Sunday's meeting with Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

#1641. Origi recalls how Milan tenure turned sour: “We weren’t on the same page”

Divock Origi has discussed what went wrong during his time at AC Milan, from the injuries to the Rossoneri’s decision to exclude him.

Origi joined Milan after the Scudetto season, i.e. the summer of 2022, and the idea was that he would be able to alternate with Olivier Giroud. However, a couple of injuries made his start difficult and it only went downhill from there.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Despite making 36 appearances in his first season, he got just two goals and was thus sent out on loan for the next season, joining Nottingham Forest. One goal and one assist later, he returned to Milan, where it was quickly decided that he was no longer part of the project.

Instead of taking the opportunity to continue his career elsewhere, Origi decided to stay and train on his own. His hefty salary of €4m net (€5.24m gross) frustrated Milan and in December 2025, they finally got the striker to terminate his contract six months earlier than its expiration.

In short, it was a costly deal for Milan and for Origi, the move effectively killed his career. Speaking to the Belgian outlet HLN.be, as cited by MilanPress, the former striker explained what happened and why he then decided to retire (in the summer of 2026).

“At 27, my time at Liverpool was over. Sometimes you need to step out of your comfort zone and take on a new challenge. It’s the only way to grow as a person. AC Milan was a very interesting project.

“Paolo Maldini signed me and I felt he truly believed in me. It’s just that I got injured. Usually, I work on my preparation with my personal trainer, but this time it didn’t work. I lost much of my basic fitness; it was difficult.”

“I don’t take it personally. It was a professional decision. Was I happy about it? Obviously not. But can I understand it? Yes. I was left out of the squad for a while and wasn’t allowed to train with the first team.

“There was the option of joining the youth team. I can’t say too much about some things for contractual reasons… Let’s just say we weren’t on the same page about it. My experience helped me keep a clear head.

“I was convinced that if you have the right intentions, everything will work out for the best in the end.”

“I had options in football, but for me it was also a time when I was starting to think about my future away from the sport. Don’t get me wrong, I’ve always dedicated myself body and soul to football. It was my great passion, ” he stated.

#1639. England 2-1 Croatia PLAYER RATINGS: Whose position is under 'serious' threat? Which two regulars need to show more? And who was at the heart of Three Lions' best attacking play?

Published: 17:06 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:16 EST, 12 November 2026

Harry Kane scored on his record 126th appearance for England as they beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley in the Nations League.

The Bayern Munich striker, 33, scored his 92nd goal for the Three Lions from the penalty spot to give them the victory.

Morgan Rogers had opened the scoring in the first half before Petar Sucic equalised.

Thomas Tuchel's side go to Spain on Sunday, where they will be in a shoot-out to qualify for the League A finals.

CRAIG HOPE was at Wembley to bring you our player ratings.

Harry Kane scored on his landmark 126th England outing to give them a 2-1 win over Croatia

Was left exposed for goal and not much he could do. Made four fairly routine saves and kicking was fine. Tuchel says he’s the No.1 but that will only become apparent should he start in Spain on Sunday. It feels like his position is under serious threat from James Trafford, not that he did anything wrong here.

A very bright start, including one delightful drop in behind for Rogers, but he faded thereafter. Not the creative force he should be in a game like this and questions remain over both Alexander-Arnold’s current level of performance and whether anyone will emerge as England’s first-choice right back.

He was enjoying a trouble-free night until mistake leading to Croatia equaliser with baffling decision to head back to Pickford amid crowded goalmouth. He did, in part, make amends by winning penalty for Kane goal, as well as timely late slide to block shot. Doesn’t convince as a starter, though.

Like Quansah, all was going well until Croatia goal, and he’ll be disappointed not to get the first header on the corner before ball dropped. He looked shaky after that and was nearly outdone for a Croatia equaliser late on. Could have done with a breather after 70 minutes or so given recent return from injury.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was not the creative force he should have been in a game like this

In a position that is up for grabs he did his chances no harm at all and was the pick of the backline by far. Got forward at every opportunity and rarely wasted a ball. Was also there at the other end with several key interceptions. A solid night.

A lot of huff and puff but, as too often in an England shirt, not enough to show for it by way of creation or penetration. With some bright young midfielders like James Garner and Alex Scott emerging, Rice has to do more, you feel, to make sure he stays in the XI. This was an underwhelming night in that regard.

Lots of involvement and omnipresent across the park, as ever. One superb dribble that drew applause, but we need to see more of that inspiration higher up the pitch. A good display, but no chances created. Partnership with Rice still feels a little forced at times.

Morgan Rogers was his team's brightest player when he forced the opening goal

Was already his team’s brightest player when he forced opening goal with close-range finish. Clearly a man in form and brought that brightness to this stage. With doubts over Saka’s durability, he looks the best bet as the starting right winger. Was at the heart of all good about England in final third.

Provided assist with confident cushion for pal Rogers and he was a threat throughout, even if final shot or pass didn’t quite come off, the assist apart. Felt like he was in second gear a little, especially knowing booking would have ruled him out of Spain on Sunday in his home city of Madrid.

Didn’t happen for Barcelona winger and he’ll know he should have done better when twice cutting in on right foot and having a good sight at goal. He missed the target on both occasions. Gordon can’t get cosy knowing he’s Tuchel’s first choice on the left, and more is needed.

Anthony Gordon will know he should have done better - he can't get cosy on the left flank

The quarterback! Was this a glimpse of the future? Kane operated even deeper than he usually does at times and one long-range pass from 30 yards inside his own half drew gasps from the Wembley crowd. It was his playmaker’s dink in behind that led to opener. Got his goal with penalty dink on his big night.

Ben White (on for Alexander-Arnold 78) - 6

A win, but it was not comfortable and Tuchel leaves this with yet more questions about how he builds a defence for the European Championship. A sold-out Wembley weren’t exactly thrilled by England’s attack, either. Job done, but it was dull.

#1636. Report: Decision made, Liverpool ready to agree £55m deal today

Liverpool are ready to strike a major deal today. Unfortunately, they'll be forced to wait to complete this one.

Liverpool spent an enormous amount of money over the last few years, with sporting director Richard Hughes moving the club away from "smart" signings and towards "big" signings. It's a strategy that hasn't worked out.

We know that because despite spending half a billion pounds, this isn't a team that particularly works. Liverpool need more signings if they're to move forward and need them in virtually every area of the pitch.

That will naturally cost a lot more money. Hopefully, the Reds are a bit smarter about this and look for a different kind of signing than the €100m+ deals which have proved problematic thus far.

One such deal is already on the cards, in fact, and reports indicate that Liverpool are ready to strike it now. Though, they'll be made to wait.

One of the most interesting deals Liverpool did strike under Hughes was for Ronald Araujo. Liverpool haven’t been one for massive loan deals in the past but they agreed one here.

Araujo joined for the season from Barcelona and has started life at Anfield wonderfully. He’s starting at right-back for now but is a natural centre-back, offering proper versatility and options in the back line.

Above all, though, he’s just playing well. It opens the door to buying him permanently, with a buy clause in his deal for a proper transfer. Liverpool just need to offer around €55m.

Marca reports that they’re ready to do just that. Araujo has impressed so much that as things stand, Liverpool want to trigger the clause and sign the Uruayan permanently.

All that’s really holding things back is the fact that the clause can’t be triggered until the end of the season. Though, that’s probably a good thing - Liverpool shouldn’t really rush here as there’s no real need. Get a full season out of Araujo and then assess the situation.

But things are heading in one direction, it seems. And that would mean many more years of Araujo.

Mo Salah's regen is coming to Liverpool's first-team. The Reds have already found him.

For much of last summer, the conversation focused on Richard Hughes' plans to replace the club legend. Liverpool knew Salah was leaving after agreeing to cancel the final year of his contract in January.

There was a plan in place. The club already had the perfect replacement lined-up. Yan Diomande had talked up his father's love for Liverpool.

The Ivorian was putting in some breathtaking performances at RB Leipzig, a club from where Liverpool have brought in a fair few players over the last half a decade.

And yet - the move didn't happen. Diomande opted to reject the Reds. He wanted the allure of Paris and later Madrid.

How Liverpool planned to replace Mo SalahAmid Diomande's rejection, there was a final frantic scramble towards the end of the summer window. Liverpool made offers for Ismaila Sarr and Yankuba Minteh. They signed two left-wingers in Victor Munoz, Bradley Barcola to add to their existing duo of Cody Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha. #1631. Prince William leads tributes to Harry Kane as England captain breaks appearance record with 126th cap: Royal presents star with shirt marking occasion as Wembley celebrates milestone

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 14:45 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:17 EST, 12 November 2026

Prince William led tributes for Harry Kane as Wembley honoured the England captain on reaching his record-breaking 126th cap against Croatia on Thursday.

Kane, who became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or last month, celebrated another remarkable feat as he surpassed legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history.

After walking out with his four children for kick-off, followed by his England team-mates, the Bayern Munich forward first held his Ballon d'Or trophy aloft to Wembley's buoyant crowd, soaking up the celebrations.

Shilton approached the England captain to present him with a medal displaying his achievement, before Kane's former Spurs team-mate Luka Modric continued the tributes by offering him another gift.

Prince William then walked on to the pitch to shake Kane's hand and present him with a framed shirt, bearing the words 'Kane 126'.

As well as holding the record for England's most capped player, the 33-year-old striker is also England's highest ever scorer with 91 goals, ahead of Wayne Rooney and Sir Bobby Charlton who netted 53 and 49 respectively during their careers.

Prince William shakes Harry Kane's hand as he celebrates the England captain's record cap

The Prince led tributes as Wembley honoured Kane ahead of England's clash with Croatia

Kane, accompanied by his four children on the pitch, held his Ballon d'Or aloft to supporters

Prince William applauded 'brilliant and remarkable' Kane on his Ballon d'Or triumph with a personal social media message after the ceremony in London.

The Prince of Wales, signing his message off with his personal 'W' initial, posted on Instagram: 'Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or! What a fantastic achievement and so deserved.

'A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.'

Kane, who has been widely regarded as a model professional and humble superstar during his career, admitted he still has an ego of sorts in an interview on the eve of his record-breaking England cap.

Asked if he has an ego, Kane replied: ‘That's a great question. I’m sure my wife will be able to say a thing or two!

'But ego is funny, because ego is many different things. I guess I have an ego to be the best, because I want to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

On becoming England's highest appearance maker, he joked that some of his current Three Lions team-mates might catch his total by the end of their careers.

‘Jude (Bellingham) and Declan (Rice), they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are,’ he added. ‘So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! The goal record is going to be the one that's difficult to beat. I think that’s good!

He has passed Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history - with 126 to his name

Kane receives a gift from ex-Spurs team-mate and fellow Ballon d'Or winner Luka Modric
